seed_rationale: S1: intermediate judgment - installing, changing over, debugging and commissioning production equipment is predominantly physical work, with a real but non-dominant informational component in control software, recipe parameters and data-driven fault diagnosis; S2: intermediate judgment - once equipment is installed, run-and-measure iteration on settings resolves within a shift, faster than the weeks-to-months anchor, but every hardware, fixture or layout change and its validation run takes days and queues on line availability, so the ordinary loop sits between the two anchors; S3 cost: intermediate judgment - each attempt consumes line time, material and skilled labour, so the marginal cost is material rather than near-free, yet attempts are frequent and repeatable rather than scarce, which lifts the coding off the bottom anchor; S3 throughput: parallelism is essentially absent because commissioning attempts are made on the one line being brought up and are strictly serial, and that is what holds the coding below the repeatable-with-constrained-throughput anchor; S4: installation, changeover and equipment settling create meaningful and unavoidable delay, but no single construction, curing, growth or qualification floor dominates the scoped stage; S5: intermediate judgment - ordinary commissioning errors cost line time and scrapped material and are containable, but a material subset, including tool collisions, equipment damage and operator-safety events, is expensive and partly irreversible, which places the stage below the containable-error anchor; scope caveat: frozen V1 scope is line installation, changeover, debug and commissioning for product introduction and ramp; it excludes upstream design and post-release production; critical_path_role remains not_assessed.
independent_rationale: S1: 1 — Intermediate judgment: diagnostics and debugging are informational, but installation, changeover, and physical line operation dominate the stage; S2: 2 — commissioning learn-test-revise cycles are generally weeks to months; S3 cost: 1 — Intermediate judgment: each line trial consumes downtime, material, and specialist labor, above the repeatable constrained anchor; S3 throughput: shared equipment makes most commissioning attempts serial even when analysis is parallel; S4: 1 — Intermediate judgment: physical installation and equipment cycling dominate much of elapsed time, while debugging remains accelerable; S5: 1 — Intermediate judgment: errors may damage equipment or create safety and ramp risks, though shutdown and rework often contain them; scope caveat: excludes ongoing production after line release.
